transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-30 15:00 PST | Duration: 55 minutes | Attendees: Alice Martinez (Redwood AE), Ben Cho (Redwood SE), Dr. Maya Patel (CISO, AcmeHealth), Liam O'Connor (Platform Eng), Ravi Singh (IT Ops)

[00:00] Alice Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Alice, AE on the account. Ben from our solutions team is here too, we'll do a quick intro then dive into SSO and RBAC.
[00:18] Ben Cho: Hi all, Ben Cho, engineering. I'll mostly cover SAML, SCIM, and RBAC patterns — happy to go deep on cert/key rotation, KMS options.
[00:30] Dr. Maya Patel: Thanks, Alice, Ben. We wanted to make sure Redwood's SSO and provisioning approach meets our audit and least-privilege requirements. We're under a tight timeline for vendor onboarding — hoping to finish security sign-off in two weeks.
[00:48] Alice Martinez: Understood. We'll try to be concise. Quick ask: can you confirm who owns SAML IdP side at AcmeHealth?
[00:55] Liam O'Connor: That's us — platform. We run Okta for most apps, but have a secondary IdP for some B2B integrations. We'll likely use Okta for the PoC.
[01:10] Ravi Singh: From ops side, we care about audit logs, retention, and KMS/BYOK. We want customer-managed keys if possible.
[01:20] Ben Cho: Great. For SSO we support SAML 2.0 for SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows. We also support SCIM 2.0 for provisioning. Typical flow: you provide IdP metadata and we provide SP metadata. SCIM can push users/groups or we can do just-in-time provisioning depending on preference.
[01:40] Dr. Maya Patel: How do you handle group-to-role mapping? We need least-privilege roles mapped to AD groups.
[01:48] Ben Cho: We recommend explicit group-to-role mapping: create RBAC roles in Redwood Console (admin, dev, billing, read-only) and map Okta groups to those roles via SCIM or via SAML assertions. SCIM is better for provisioning (creates users and adds them to groups), while SAML group claims work for session-time authorization.
[02:10] Liam O'Connor: If a user is removed from Okta, how fast does Redwood revoke access? We need near-immediate de-provisioning for SSO-disabled users.
[02:22] Ben Cho: With SCIM provisioning, deprovision events are pushed immediately and access is revoked within a minute or two server-side. With just SAML claims, you'd rely on session expiry unless you trigger a manual session revoke via API.
[02:36] Dr. Maya Patel: Okay, SCIM then. What about SCIM attribute mappings? We need to sync title, department, and manager for access review.
[02:46] Ben Cho: We'll share a SCIM schema example. We map userName, externalId, name.givenName, name.familyName, emails, and groups. Additional custom attributes can be added as extension attrs in SCIM if you need manager or department.
[03:05] Ravi Singh: Do you have SCIM throttling limits? We batch-provision large directories.
[03:12] Ben Cho: We rate-limit SCIM to protect endpoints; typical enterprise customers do periodic full syncs and then incremental deltas. We'll include recommended throttling config in the guide.
[03:30] Alice Martinez: Switching to RBAC: Ben, can you walk through least-privilege patterns and a recommended role set for platform teams?
[03:40] Ben Cho: Sure. Start with narrow roles: platform-viewer (read-only), platform-operator (deploy, monitor), model-admin (deploy models, change variants), billing-admin. Avoid giving devs model-admin by default. Use groups for temporary elevated access and require ticket-based approval for role grants.
[04:00] Dr. Maya Patel: And approvals — does Redwood support SSO-based MFA enforcement and conditional access?
[04:06] Ben Cho: Yes, SAML SSO follows your IdP policies — if Okta enforces MFA or device checks, those carry through. For step-up auth inside the console we can integrate with session policies and IP allowlists for sensitive actions.
[04:24] Liam O'Connor: About keys — BYOK options? We don't want Redwood managing the root keys for production workloads.
[04:30] Ben Cho: We support customer-managed KMS in hosted and private deployments. For hosted, we offer an integration path where you create a key in your cloud KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and grant Redwood a restricted HSM-wrapped key or use an HSM proxy for signing. For private/on-prem, you can host the key material entirely in your HSM.
[04:54] Ravi Singh: Any hurdles for HSM-backed keys with Redwood Dedicated?
[04:58] Ben Cho: We have a flow for Dedicated that allows HSM integration; you'll need network peering and our certs for mutual TLS. We'll document the setup.
[05:09] Dr. Maya Patel: Audit logs — what do they capture and how long are they retained? We need immutable audit trails for at least 12 months for now.
[05:18] Ben Cho: Audit logs capture sign-ins, role changes, API calls, model deployments, and key rotations. Default retention in hosted is 90 days; we offer extended retention add-ons up to multi-year depending on your plan. We can also stream logs to your SIEM via syslog or cloud logging sinks.
[05:38] Liam O'Connor: Can we get read-only copies of logs exported daily to our S3 bucket?
[05:42] Ben Cho: Yes, we support daily exports to customer S3/GCS/Azure blob in encrypted form. We'll include the export format in the docs.
[05:52] Alice Martinez: Data residency — you're in EU and US, right?
[05:56] Liam O'Connor: We need EU residency for PHI-adjacent data; vendor must support region isolation.
[06:05] Ben Cho: Redwood supports region pinning for data residency. For regulated workloads we recommend Private deployment (VPC or on-prem). Hosted can be region-limited for data at rest but Private gives strongest guarantees.
[06:20] Dr. Maya Patel: Is there a DPA template and data processing addendum?
[06:25] Alice Martinez: Yes, I'll send the DPA and standard contract redlines. We'll include privacy and subprocessors list.
[06:32] Ravi Singh: What about encryption in transit?
[06:35] Ben Cho: All traffic is TLS 1.2+ with mTLS options for inter-service comms in private deployments. At-rest encryption uses cloud KMS by default and can be BYOK as discussed.
[06:46] Dr. Maya Patel: Certificate rotation — can operations trigger key rotations and how do you handle rollbacks?
[06:52] Ben Cho: We support key rotation APIs and have automated multi-stage rotation to avoid downtime. Rollbacks are possible but require careful steps; we'll provide runbooks.
[07:06] Liam O'Connor: For SCIM provisioning, do you support SCIM group nesting? Our org has nested groups.
[07:12] Ben Cho: SCIM v2 doesn't natively support nested groups; we recommend flattening or provisioning a mapping layer in Okta. We'll share best practices we use with other health customers.
[07:28] Dr. Maya Patel: Regarding SOC2/ISO, can you provide the most recent reports and the scope? Particularly whether Redwood's private deployments are included.
[07:36] Alice Martinez: Yes, we have SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001 coverage. For Private (customer-managed) deployments, some controls change — we'll annotate which controls remain in-scope. I'll share the security binder after the call.
[07:50] Ravi Singh: Are there any penetration test or vulnerability disclosure programs?
[07:55] Ben Cho: We run quarterly pen tests and have a coordinated vulnerability disclosure program. We can share redacted reports and scope.
[08:04] Liam O'Connor: A couple of edge cases: can you restrict console access to specific IP ranges and require VPN?
[08:11] Ben Cho: Yes, we support IP allowlists per org and can require VPC peering for private control plane. You can also set session timeouts and require MFA via IdP.
[08:24] Alice Martinez: Time check — we've covered the big ones. Any specific technical demos you want next?
[08:30] Liam O'Connor: We'd like a hands-on RBAC workshop — mapping our Okta groups to roles and validating deprovisioning. Possibly a short SAML test.
[08:40] Dr. Maya Patel: And a review of KMS BYOK flow with our security team.
[08:45] Ben Cho: We'll propose two next sessions: 1) RBAC/SCIM workshop with platform and ops (50–60m) and 2) KMS/BYOK deep dive (30m).
[08:56] Alice Martinez: I'll follow up with calendar invites and send the docs: SOC2, ISO summary, DPA, SAML/SCIM guides, and RBAC templates.
[09:05] Dr. Maya Patel: Sounds good. A nit: we've had issues with some vendors where audit logs were incomplete for certain admin actions. Can you confirm model deployment events include the user and rollback history?
[09:18] Ben Cho: Yes, deployments include user ID, timestamp, model version, and rollback events are tracked in the audit trail. We'll highlight which API calls map to which audit events.
[09:32] Liam O'Connor: Can you show an example of the RBAC JSON or YAML you expect us to import?
[09:38] Ben Cho: I'll attach a sample role mapping JSON. It includes role name, allowed actions, resource scoping (org/project/model), and expiration for temporary grants.
[09:50] Ravi Singh: For temporary elevated access, can roles be auto-expiring?
[09:54] Ben Cho: Yes, we support time-limited role grants with automatic revocation. Good for break-glass or short-term vendor access.
[10:05] Alice Martinez: Okay we'll wrap with next steps recap.
[10:08] Dr. Maya Patel: Quick clarification — SCIM provisioning for group members only, or do you create user accounts too?
[10:15] Ben Cho: We can both create users and manage group membership. If you already provision centrally, you can choose group-only sync.
[10:24] Alice Martinez: Recap of agreed items: use Okta + SCIM for immediate deprovisioning, RBAC mapping via group-to-role, customer-managed KMS for prod, extended audit log retention export to S3, and share security docs.
[10:40] Liam O'Connor: That matches our expectations. We'll prepare Okta metadata and group list.
[10:46] Ravi Singh: We'll also pull legal contacts for the DPA.
[10:50] Alice Martinez: Thanks everyone — we'll send the materials today and propose times for the workshops.
[10:58] Dr. Maya Patel: Appreciate it.
[11:02] Ben Cho: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the SCIM and RBAC artifacts.
[11:08] Alice Martinez: Meeting adjourned.

Notes: transcription contains occasional minor mis-hears (e.g., "KV cash" instead of KV cache). References to product names: Redwood Dedicated, Redwood Private, Redwood Console. Shared artifacts referenced: security binder (link to be provided), SCIM/SAML configuration guide (link), RBAC sample JSON (attachment).

Action items (as discussed above) and next steps reiterated in metadata.
